observations.summary: Directory-path guarantees are unpinned by owner tests: G5b (directory created before the reservation) passes the owner's test and leaves a directory under a {1,1,1} ledger that returns Budget (the 453 RF-1 class on the new path); G6 (security name check removed) passes and the platform then refuses only after the full charge. Mirror the file tests for directories: unpaid -> Budget with nothing created; bad names -> Name with zero charge; existing entry/symlink -> AlreadyExists; inheriting parent -> Access with nothing appended. Before any caller.

mkdirat then openat by name leaves a window; the SAFETY comment's 'the name still refers to the directory just created' is an unverified semantic assumption. fchmod (EPERM) and private_shape (owner/mode) stop a foreign-owned substitute, but a same-owner, possibly non-empty directory would be accepted. After openat verify freshness (owner = euid, link count 2, empty) and reword SAFETY.

create_private_regular_file_cost() {1 object, 1 edge, 0 bytes} ('one exclusive create of an empty regular file') is reused for directories (mkdirat + openat + fchmod = 3 native calls); the file path is 2 calls (openat + fchmod), which the reviewer missed at 453 r2. Capture/append costs count calls exactly; define separate documented file (2 edges) and directory (3 edges) create costs.
The directory fchmod is unpinned (G1): caught only under a restrictive umask with an explicit-mode fixture (reviewer evidence: mode 500 without it under umask 0277).
single_component's error text says 'invalid private file name' and is now shared with directories.

Residual entry after refusal and retry AlreadyExists; public unaccounted create_exclusive_* platform writes; openat mode style nit on the file path; unused From impls and nested WorkFailure in Capture/Append.
